objections.claim: FY2017 contains 378 duplicate rows across 7 source tables
International Business Machines Corporation first appears in FY2017 with no prior facts
The reported Services net income jump has no real component; corrected series shows opposite direction
Oracle Corporation is the fastest-growing filer in Services (0.929x FY2016 to FY2017) and accounts for 7.3% of the reported jump
Zetaris holds 39 International Business Machines Corporation facts; the SEC endpoint returns 39, so no data is missing

args.question: is the FY2017 Services net income jump real?
args.finding:
Verdict: DATA_ARTIFACT (filing_year_duplication=100.0%)
- FY2017 holds 89 rows across 34 distinct period_end dates; 378 duplicate rows across the 7 source tables.
- International Business Machines Corporation first appears in fiscal_year 2017 (39 facts across 3 fiscal years, none in FY2016); that contributes $67.8B of the $63.2B jump. Scout found the earlier periods under ProfitLoss (16 annual 10-K facts).
- Corrected Services moved the other way (-$12.0B, 0.438x); the reported jump has no real component. SEC frames parity 10/10.
- Oracle Corporation is the fastest-growing filer in Services (0.929x FY2016 to FY2017), but its -$4.6B is only 7.3% of the reported jump.
- Zetaris holds 39 International Business Machines Corporation facts; the SEC companyconcept endpoint returns 39. Nothing is missing.
Note: concept_switch_missing_history is confirmed as a data-quality finding but carries no separate share: deduplicating to one annual fact per (cik, period_end) recovers International Business Machines Corporation's prior-year facts, so it does not add to the reported jump.
Note: Eliminated with exhibits, not left as possibilities: real_change, single_filer_growth, ingestion_gap.
Note: Defense Counsel raised 5 objection(s); the deterministic code gate is final.
Note: SAMPLE_MODE: tool results replayed from the labelled cassette; no live inference.

statements: CREATE SCHEMASTORE CONTAINER exhibit_a_shadow

CREATE OR REPLACE SCHEMASTORE VIEW sector_net_income_by_year WITH CONTAINER exhibit_a_shadow AS WITH annual AS (
  SELECT
    s.sic_division,
    f.cik,
    f.period_start,
    f.period_end,
    f.value_usd,
    f.filed_date,
    CASE
      WHEN MONTH(f.period_end) <= 6 THEN YEAR(f.period_end) - 1
      ELSE YEAR(f.period_end)
    END AS period_year,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY f.cik, f.period_end
      ORDER BY f.filed_date DESC, f.value_usd DESC
    ) AS rn
  FROM (
    SELECT * FROM edgar.apple_netincome_table
    UNION ALL SELECT * FROM edgar.ibm_netincome_table
    UNION ALL SELECT * FROM edgar.oracle_netincome_table
    UNION ALL SELECT * FROM edgar.walmart_netincome_table
    UNION ALL SELECT * FROM edgar.target_netincome_table
    UNION ALL SELECT * FROM edgar.ford_netincome_table
    UNION ALL SELECT * FROM edgar.tesla_netincome_table
  ) f
  LEFT JOIN edgar.sic_edgar_usl s ON s.cik = f.cik
  WHERE DATEDIFF(f.period_end, f.period_start) BETWEEN 330 AND 400
)
SELECT
  sic_division,
  period_year AS fiscal_year,
  SUM(value_usd) AS net_income_usd
FROM annual
WHERE rn = 1
  AND period_year BETWEEN 2016 AND 2019
GROUP BY sic_division, period_year

hypotheses.statement: The 2017 movement in Services is inflated because analytics.sector_net_income_by_year sums value_usd grouped by the filing's fiscal_year, so prior-year comparatives, quarterly facts and year-to-date facts are counted again under the later filing year.
hypotheses.note: FY2017 holds 89 rows across 34 distinct period_end dates; 378 duplicate rows across the 7 source tables.

hypotheses.statement: The 2017 bucket gains a filer that is absent from 2016, because a filer's Revenues concept stops after one filing and its whole fact history lands in a single fiscal_year.
hypotheses.note: International Business Machines Corporation first appears in fiscal_year 2017 (39 facts across 3 fiscal years, none in FY2016); that contributes $67.8B of the $63.2B jump. Scout found the earlier periods under ProfitLoss (16 annual 10-K facts).

hypotheses.statement: Revenue in Services genuinely grew between 2016 and 2017; the increase should survive deduplication and agree with an independent SEC frames value.
hypotheses.note: Corrected Services moved the other way (-$12.0B, 0.438x); the reported jump has no real component. SEC frames parity 10/10.

hypotheses.statement: One fast-growing filer in Services explains the 2017 movement on its own.
hypotheses.note: Oracle Corporation is the fastest-growing filer in Services (0.929x FY2016 to FY2017), but its -$4.6B is only 7.3% of the reported jump.

hypotheses.statement: The artifact is an ingestion gap: Zetaris lost facts that the SEC endpoint still returns, so the naive series is missing rows rather than duplicating them.
hypotheses.note: Zetaris holds 39 International Business Machines Corporation facts; the SEC companyconcept endpoint returns 39. Nothing is missing.

query.question: is the FY2017 Services net income jump real?

discovery.replacement_reason: NetIncomeLoss has 11 annual 10-K facts starting 2015-12-31; ProfitLoss has 16 annual 10-K facts starting 2007-12-31, so the earlier periods were filed under a different concept, not lost.
discovery.rule: NetIncomeLoss family concept must have USD annual 10-K facts (330-400 days) and either extend the current chain (ending within 421 days) or precede it

critic.detail: 5 objection(s): Each alleged cause is contradicted by evidence showing insufficient duplicate counts, prior IBM records, limited corrected series data, missing growth ratio support, and incomplete SEC record counts, indicating the reported jump lacks a sol
